rules.title: RSO allowable annual rent increase
rules.requirement: For RSO units, rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage. Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.key_value: once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage
rules.coverage_text: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, and replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28. Covered types include apartments, condominiums, townhomes, duplexes, two or more single-family dwelling units on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming/boarding house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to a commercial building, ADUs, JADUs, and mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks.
rules.exemptions: Condominium and townhome rent amounts are not regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995. Rent may be increased to market rate if the tenant voluntarily moves out, is evicted for nonpayment, lease violation, failure to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan, or per a City Attorney order, or accepts a Tenant Buyout Agreement. Landlords may apply for a Luxury Exemption.
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage

rules.title: RSO additional occupant rent increase
rules.requirement: Effective February 2, 2026, an additional 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. A 10% increase is allowed for an additional tenant (not a dependent) who moves into the unit, and the landlord can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.
rules.key_value: 10% for an additional tenant (not a dependent)
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the RSO (generally properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, and replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28).
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. However, a 10% for an additional tenant is allowed (not a dependent) if moves into a rental unit: Landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.

rules.title: RSO rent increase moratorium
rules.requirement: Rent increases were prohibited for rental units subject to the RSO from March 30, 2020, through January 31, 2024.
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 30, 2020, through January 31, 2024, rent increases are prohibited for rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

rules.title: RSO legal reasons for eviction
rules.requirement: Tenancies in RSO units may be terminated only for listed legal reasons: at-fault reasons (failure to pay rent, failure to address a rental agreement violation, nuisance or damage, illegal use, failure to renew a similar rental agreement, failure to provide reasonable access, unapproved subtenant at end of lease term) or no-fault reasons (owner or immediate family move-in, resident manager move-in, demolition and permanent removal from the rental market, government order, conversion to affordable housing).
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the RSO (generally properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, and replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28).
rules.quoted_span: Failure to fix or address a violation of the rental agreement

rules.title: Filing of termination notices with LAHD
rules.requirement: All notices to terminate a tenancy for rental units subject to the RSO must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.
rules.key_value: three (3) business days of service on the tenant
rules.coverage_text: All rental units subject to the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) within

rules.title: No-fault eviction requirements and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: No-fault evictions require payment of tenant relocation assistance, filing a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD, and giving the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension).
rules.key_value: 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension)
rules.coverage_text: No-fault evictions from rental units subject to the RSO.
rules.quoted_span: Give the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension).

rules.title: Notice of Right to Counsel
rules.requirement: Beginning August 20, 2025, landlords must post the Notice of Right to Counsel, provide it to the tenant at the start of the tenancy, and attach it to a copy of any eviction notice or termination of a rental subsidy.
rules.quoted_span: The Notice must also be attached to a copy of any eviction notice or termination of a rental subsidy.
